en.title: The verbs avoir and être
en.goal: Conjugate avoir and être in the present tense and recognize how they are used in sentences.

blocks.title: Avoir and être
blocks.body: Avoir (to have) and être (to be) are the two most-used verbs in French — and the only ones that are completely irregular in the present tense. You've already seen several of their forms in the last few units (je suis, j'ai, il a...) without stopping to think about the full conjugation.

blocks.title: No pattern to work out
blocks.body: Notice that neither conjugation follows a regular pattern — you can't "work out" the form from the infinitive, so it's worth memorizing the whole table, not just the isolated forms you've already seen.

blocks.title: A common trap
blocks.body: French uses avoir (to have) in several expressions where English uses "to be" — avoir faim (to be hungry), avoir soif (to be thirsty), avoir peur (to be afraid), avoir raison (to be right). If the English sentence uses "to be" with a feeling or state like these, chances are French uses avoir.
